description: A coalition of Nordic and Benelux states continues to deepen its informal AI crisis coordination, establishing joint incident response drills and shared red-teaming exercises that operate outside formal EU command. As central EU mechanisms stall, this parallel structure gains operational credibility and begins to attract interest from Central European members concerned about asymmetric threats.

The open-source AI-powered cyber defence toolkit spreads to regional governments and utilities across southern and eastern Europe, significantly improving patching speed and anomaly detection in under-resourced sectors. Its grassroots adoption pressures EU institutions to either regulate, endorse, or integrate it — none of which are straightforward given compliance and liability concerns.
